summary.headline: MM Forgings Q1 FY27 net sales rose to INR427 crore (+16% YoY) with EBITDA at 18% margin; management guides ~18% growth and ~INR1,800-1,900 crore FY27 turnover.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 net sales were INR427 crore against INR369 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR82 crore (about 18% margin excluding other income). PBT grew about 30%, helped by a one-time land sale gain in Oragadam, Chennai (INR64 crore gross, INR58 crore net of tax), which management excluded from the EBITDA growth figures. Volumes were about 20,200 tonnes, with management saying April and May were hit by labour shortages and June and July recovered. Management expects Q2 onwards at 23,000-25,000 tonnes per quarter, targeting over 90,000 tonnes in FY27 and 1 lakh tonnes-plus run rate.

financial_highlights.value: INR82 crore (~18% margin ex other income; INR75 crore net of other income, ~18%)
INR64 crore gross profit; INR58 crore net of tax

financial_highlights.change: vs INR1.93 lakh in previous quarter

segments.name: Geography
segments.commentary: India 63.5%, US 18% (vs ~15-16% a year earlier), Europe 14%, South America 4%, others ~1%. Europe sales fell from INR89 crore in Q1 FY26-adjacent quarter to INR59 crore now per analyst's figures; management said no business was lost.

segments.name: End-market
segments.commentary: Commercial vehicles 71%, agri and off-highway 14%, passenger car/tractor (PAT) 14%, others 1%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover expected around INR1,800-1,900 crore, about 18% growth on ~INR1,600 crore in FY26.

Quarterly sales target of 23,000-25,000 tonnes from Q2 FY27 and minimum 25,000 tonnes in the coming 2-3 quarters; later 27,000 and then 30,000 tonnes per quarter, with ~1.2 lakh tonnes capacity utilisation mentioned in closing.
FY27 volume expected to cross 90,000 tonnes, with run rate of at least 1 lakh tonnes per annum; FY28 target 1.0-1.1 lakh tonnes.
EBITDA margin: management targets 20%-plus, aiming to squeeze out 2-3% from the system, with 1-2% visibility.
FY27 capex around INR150 crore, of which INR30-50 crore replacement/debottlenecking; gross debt to be held at INR750-800 crore with repayment of ~INR170 crore offset by fresh borrowing.
Management reiterated target of INR3,000 crore revenue by FY30.
capex_capacity: 16,500-tonne forging press due for production by Q4 FY27; 4,000-tonne press commissioned in the last few weeks.
Management says all machining and forging cells ran at full capability from June; remaining 7-10% constraint is technical, with debottlenecking targeted to lift output by 15-20%.
Cumulative machining investment about INR1,100 crore, of which INR625 crore in the last 5 years and ~INR1,000 crore in the last 10 years.
Automation spend about INR7.5-10 crore to date; expected to rise to INR30-50 crore by end of FY27.
Management could not quantify machining capacity in tonnes; said it will come back with a method. Gross block ~INR2,100 crore; CNC machine count described as 'hundreds' without a figure.
demand_pricing: Management described demand as strong across domestic and export markets, with US commercial vehicle (Class 8 truck) demand moving strongly and Indian CV, tractor and passenger car markets running hot.
Realisation per tonne up to INR2.02 lakh from INR1.93 lakh; management attributed the ~350 bps sequential gross margin improvement to higher realisation and machining/export mix.
New orders are mostly machined parts, which management says raise capital requirements.
Hyperscaler-linked business is filtering into domestic forging demand; management said it is moving into businesses that support hyperscalers.
Freight costs rose sharply on routes around the Strait of Hormuz, and fuel costs spiked in Q1 due to the West Asia conflict, which has since stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year growth outlook by market, and reason for higher machining mix?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 turnover expected at INR1,800-1,900 crore (~18% growth). Machining mix expected at 65-68%, reflecting ~3 years of machining investment.

qa_highlights.question: Employee cost increase QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Increment was given from 1 April 2026 rather than in the subsequent quarter, plus some headcount additions; management expects current cost levels to hold through the year.

qa_highlights.question: Debt reduction plan and capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross debt held at ~INR750 crore; ~INR170 crore repaid and redrawn; capex ~INR150 crore. Land sale proceeds to go to working capital, capex and borrowings. No plan to raise debt beyond INR750-800 crore until turnover and EBITDA grow.

qa_highlights.question: Other expenses up 35% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: Export freight is the main driver (about INR4 crore of a INR4.2 crore increase), due to routing around the Strait of Hormuz; base overheads rose about 10% (INR8 crore to INR9 crore).

qa_highlights.question: Europe revenue decline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Europe is stable and moves with customer demand, volume-wise de-grown, with no business lost.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and inventory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is targeting lower working capital; AI tools are being used to identify slow inventory, with a rapid action team to clear stock and WIP cut to about one week.

qa_highlights.question: EBITDA margin headroom?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees scope for improvement; target 20%-plus, with 1-2% visible and 2-3% as the stretch goal.

qa_highlights.question: Tractor/axle suspension entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Not at this moment; management cited margin dilution and focus on current growth and cost reduction.

qa_highlights.question: QIP status?
qa_highlights.answer: QIP is on the cards and under consideration; to be pursued at an appropriate time linked to market opportunity.

risks_watch: Working capital and inventory build-up; management says it is actively trying to reduce it, and the timing of the reduction is not yet quantified.
Cost pressure from freight, power and fuel, and rising personnel costs following increments; management flagged cost challenges.
Labour availability: April and May volumes were hit by shortages; June recovered with hires.
Mix shift toward machined parts raises capital needs; management said most new orders are now machined.
Machining capacity remains unquantified; management promised a method at a later date.
Unresolved status of the enabling QIP resolution.
Europe revenue trend: Q2 FY26 INR82 crore, then INR89 crore, INR68 crore, and INR59 crore in Q1 FY27 per analyst's figures.
